transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I’m here because when I start eating, I can’t seem to stop. It’s like my hands just keep reaching for more, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.” That loss of control scares me.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
Yes. Sometimes after I’ve eaten too much, I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. And I’ve taken laxatives too, because I get scared that the food is going to stay in me.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food?

Yes. When I’m alone in the afternoon, I can go through a whole loaf of bread, peanut butter, cookies, leftovers, and ice cream all in one sitting. It’s a lot before I even really stop and look at what I’ve eaten.
How often do these binge-and-purge episodes happen?

For many months, it’s been at least once almost every week. Usually an afternoon where I lose control eating, then I try to undo it somehow—vomiting, laxatives, not eating, or making myself walk and do chores.

latest_inference.note: Recurrent objectively large binge episodes with loss of control plus compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, fasting/excessive activity) occurring at least weekly for many months strongly supports bulimia nervosa and rules out residual/unspecified eating disorder categories.
